profiles.meeting_scenario: At a business school's AI and Digital Innovation lab, an associate professor and a senior PhD researcher are holding a planning meeting for a 10-week ICIS paper project tentatively titled "Deep Learning for Information Systems Research: Positioning an IT Service Management Case." The paper is intended to combine a DL-ISR conceptual framing section, a coded review of prior literature, and a pilot deep-learning demonstration using anonymized enterprise help-desk ticket data from three partner firms. The agenda is to decide what goes into the literature review matrix, what counts as the pilot application area, what should be ready for the lab's mid-project internal draft on May 17, and how the reproducibility materials will be prepared. The expected outcome is a division of labor, a milestone plan, and shared confidence that the project is fully scoped for the conference timeline.

members.name: Dr. Elena Park
members.role: Associate Professor of Information Systems and project lead
members.expertise: IS theory building, digital innovation, research framing for top IS venues, conceptual synthesis
members.background: Elena is a tenured faculty member who publishes in MISQ and ISR and often leads interdisciplinary projects that translate technical methods into IS contributions.
members.private_state: She wants the project to read as a distinctly IS contribution rather than a generic applied ML paper, and she is concerned about keeping the scope tight enough to hit the ICIS deadline without losing the conceptual framing.
hidden_assumptions: A "venue review" for positioning an IS paper naturally centers on basket-of-eight journals plus major IS conferences, with adjacent CS work used only as background citations rather than coded as part of the formal matrix.
An "internal draft" is successful if the argument, framing, tableshells, and conceptual figures are coherent, even if some empirical values are still provisional.
A "reproducibility package" for a conference submission can consist of cleaned scripts, parameter settings, and a synthetic example when the real organizational data cannot be shared.
An "application area" in the KCF sense can be represented by one well-chosen organizational task, as long as the business function is clear and the theoretical positioning is explicit.

members.name: Ravi Menon
members.role: Senior PhD researcher in IS with ML methods lead responsibility
members.expertise: Deep learning experimentation, NLP for enterprise text, evaluation pipelines, computational literature mapping
members.background: Ravi has an engineering master's degree and is finishing a dissertation on machine learning in organizational settings, often serving as the technical bridge between business-school theory and model implementation.
members.private_state: He wants the project to be methodologically airtight and reusable for later journal submission, and he worries that conceptual work will outrun what the empirical pipeline can actually support.
hidden_assumptions: A convincing "venue review" should include adjacent outlets such as KDD, AAAI, CHI, and management analytics venues when those papers shape what IS reviewers will compare against.
An "internal draft" sent to the lab should already contain stable result tables and appendix details, because otherwise feedback on the empirical section becomes noisy and wasted.
A proper "reproducibility package" means the whole experiment can be rerun end-to-end in a controlled environment, ideally via Docker on the secure server using the exact data snapshot.

An "application area" like IT service management usually includes more than one closely related task variant, such as ticket routing and escalation prediction, because that is what makes the case feel representative rather than anecdotal.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the venue review matrix
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to build the "review matrix" or "venue review" for prior DL-ISR work.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes the formal coded review will cover AIS basket journals and core IS conferences from 2018 onward, while non-IS technical papers will appear only in narrative framing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes the matrix will also code adjacent ML, HCI, and analytics papers that IS scholars regularly cite, including KDD, AAAI, CHI, and DSS-style outlets.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see themselves as broadening and strengthening the literature section, and "review matrix" sounds specific enough that neither expects the inclusion boundary to need spelling out.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the May 17 internal draft
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both commit to having an "internal draft" ready for the lab meeting on May 17.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the milestone is met if the paper has polished framing, section text, figure drafts, and placeholder or preliminary empirical tables that can still change after feedback.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the milestone is met only if the main empirical tables, appendix details, and run settings are already stable enough that later changes will be minor.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In academic planning, "internal draft" usually sounds like a routine milestone, and both are experienced enough that each assumes their own lab norm is the obvious one.

misalignment_points.topic: How the reproducibility package will be prepared
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to "package the pipeline" so the work is reproducible for later review and extension.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes this means organizing training scripts, hyperparameter logs, and a synthetic toy example, with a methods appendix explaining anything that depends on restricted partner data.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes this means building a Dockerized end-to-end workflow on the secure cluster that can rerun preprocessing, training, and evaluation from the exact frozen data snapshot.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They fully agree on the goal of reproducibility, but each imports a different default method from their own community, and the phrase "package the pipeline" hides the execution gap.

misalignment_points.topic: What the IT service management application area includes
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use "the ITSM application area" or "the support-ticket case" for the pilot demonstration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means one focal task within IT service management—classifying inbound help-desk tickets—because that is enough to instantiate the business function by application-area logic in the paper.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a broader support-ticket case covering both routing and escalation prediction, since both belong to the same operational application area and make the pilot look more representative.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds highly concrete, and both are talking about the same partner data and organizational setting, so the difference between one task and two task variants remains invisible.
